requirement:
An mdBook chapter MAY declare a named definition using a fenced `{definition}` directive. Definitions MUST use the same chapter-qualified names, identifier rules, fence rules, and nonempty-body rules as requirements and examples. Names MUST be unique across all three kinds.

Each definition MUST declare exactly one nonempty `:phrase:` option before its explanatory body. The phrase MUST be interpreted as plain text. Definitions MUST NOT require their own evidence records or determinations.
rationale:
**Verdict:** the implementation covers each obligation of `requirements.definitions.declaration`, the {impl} marking is complete, and the tests cover the main points in the design space. I found no acknowledged FIXMEs and no unmarked gaps.

**Implementation**
- **Directive recognition and shared rules.** `definition_blocks` (src/lib.rs) recognises `{definition}` alongside `{req}` and `{example}`. It uses the same colon-fence handling (`colon_fence`, closing fence length), the same `valid_name` identifier check, and the same Markdown code-range protection. `collect_definitions` (src/evidence.rs) applies `full_requirement_name` chapter qualification and `valid_name`, and reports a missing closing fence and empty text for all three kinds.
- **Uniqueness across kinds.** `collect_definitions` keeps one `BTreeMap` for all kinds and reports "duplicate {kind} {name}; first declared at …" on collision. `preprocess_book` also keeps one map, so the first declaration wins when rendering.
- **Exactly one nonempty `:phrase:` before a nonempty body.** `terms::declaration` (src/terms.rs) rejects four cases: a missing or empty `:phrase:`, a phrase that is not the first line, a missing body, and a duplicate `:phrase:` immediately after the first. `collect_definitions` calls it for every definition and reports "definition {name}: …".
- **Phrase as plain text.** `terms::escaped_phrase` entity-escapes Markdown and HTML metacharacters. `replace_definitions` and the term-reference rewriting use it, so the phrase renders literally.
- **No evidence records or determinations.** `inspect_repository_with_progress` skips `DefinitionKind::Term` for the evidence-coverage check and for matching evidence files. `validate_references` excludes terms from the evidence subjects and from `{impl}`/`{test}`/`{cite}` targets. Other term exclusions — in authoring, status, and Rust-item coverage — appear in `src/commands.rs`, `src/authoring/batch.rs`, `src/authoring/inputs.rs`, `src/inputs.rs`, `src/authoring/tools.rs` and `src/rust_coverage.rs`. They are covered by other requirements (`definitions.selection`, `references.rust_item_coverage`, `authoring.batch`). They are not part of this requirement's declaration obligations, so I did not count them as unmarked partial implementations.
- **Rendering helpers.** `DefinitionKind::noun` and `DefinitionKind::badge` carry the `definition` labels, and `reference_roles` protects the term phrase line from being parsed as a reference. All are marked {impl} for this requirement.

**Tests** (tests/definitions.rs)
- `invalid_declarations_and_reference_targets_are_reported` covers five failures:
  - a body with no `:phrase:`;
  - an empty phrase;
  - a duplicate phrase;
  - a phrase with no body;
  - an unclosed fence.
  
  It also covers a duplicate name between a requirement and a definition, and term references to missing or wrong-kind targets.
- `phrases_are_plain_links_and_markdown_literals_are_preserved` covers phrase escaping, that `:phrase:` is stripped from rendered output, and that the anchor is present.
- The fixture and `cyclic_dependencies_are_captured_once_and_changes_require_review` show that definitions with no evidence files validate with no errors. That test asserts `validate_repository(root).unwrap().errors.is_empty()` while the glossary definitions have no evidence records.

**Minor gaps, not enough to fail:** invalid-name handling and example-versus-definition duplicates are not tested for definitions specifically. They go through the shared code paths used by requirements and examples.

An mdBook chapter MAY declare a named definition using a fenced `{definition}` directive. Definitions MUST use the same chapter-qualified names, identifier rules, fence rules, and nonempty-body rules as requirements and examples. Names MUST be unique across all three kinds.

Each definition MUST declare exactly one nonempty `:phrase:` option before its explanatory body. The phrase MUST be interpreted as plain text. Definitions MUST NOT require their own evidence records or determinations.

The `{term}` role followed by a backtick-delimited full definition name MUST reference a named definition. In rendered Markdown, the reference MUST display the definition's phrase as an ordinary hyperlink to its anchored declaration, without a badge. The phrase MUST be escaped appropriately for rendering.

Missing targets and targets of another kind MUST be reported. Escaped references and references in Markdown code examples MUST remain literal. A term reference MUST NOT satisfy a requirement citation or a Rust function's requirement-coverage obligation.

Validation MUST reject missing definitions and changed snapshot text, identifying the definition and showing a compact diff when available. Moving an unchanged definition within its chapter MUST NOT invalidate its snapshot. Evidence displays MUST show the definition name, current source location, and recorded text.
Requirement and example evidence MUST include a definition input for every term referenced by its subject text or reviewed inputs.

Habeas MUST repeatedly include definitions referenced by required definitions until the set reaches a fixed point. Each required definition MUST have exactly one definition input per evidence record. Cyclic references MUST be permitted and MUST NOT cause repeated expansion or nontermination.
Validation MUST report missing required definition inputs and MUST NOT silently refresh snapshots.

A {term}`requirements.references.definition_selection` in a requirements input MUST continue to select requirements and named examples, excluding named definitions. Definitions referenced by selected texts MUST be captured as separate definition inputs, regardless of whether their names match the selection. Sharing a selection's matching name prefix alone MUST NOT make a definition a dependency.

A requirements input selects `requirements.cli.*`. A selected requirement references `glossary.command`, which is captured as a separate definition input despite not matching that selection. An unreferenced definition named `requirements.cli.unrelated` is not selected merely because its name matches the selection. {cite}`requirements.definitions.selection`

An evidence record has determination true and a current definition input. After the definition changes, validation reports stale evidence without modifying the record. Running `habeas add-input` for that record refreshes its required definition input and leaves determination false pending review. {cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs` {cite}`requirements.definitions.capture`

In a book chapter, each valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference MUST render as a Shields.io static badge image with meaningful alt text that displays its role and full name and links to the badge at the corresponding `{req}` or `{example}` definition. Links MUST work across chapters, including nested chapters. Each fenced `{req}` or `{example}` directive MUST render as a Shields.io definition badge image identifying its kind; text outside a directive MUST remain literal. Badge text MUST remain legible regardless of whether its link has been visited. These badges use the syntax defined by {cite}`requirements.references.targets`.

For every `{impl}` and `{test}` reference in a project source file, including one in a requirement or example declaration, the evidence file for the referenced requirement or example MUST contain an input whose resolved source ranges cover the reference's file and line. A `{cite}` reference MUST NOT require coverage; it is discoverable through {cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`. Habeas MUST report every uncovered reference with its role, full name, source file, and line number.

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file in the project. Every explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and every struct, enum, and union MUST have a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body. A comment immediately preceding an item's declaration or its attributes is attached to that item. A comment within an item's body, including one before a field, variant, or attribute inside it, belongs to the smallest enclosing item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report every unreferenced item with its file, line, kind, and name, and MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file.
